name: Cloudflare Registrar
summary: Cloudflare Registrar is where you buy your own web address at the same wholesale price Cloudflare pays, with no markup.

free_plan_covers.note: Cloudflare Registrar has no free plan; every domain is a paid purchase billed once a year.

first_paid_usd_month.note: There's no monthly plan; domains are billed once a year at renewal, not monthly.

portability.note: Transferring out uses a normal auth code with no Cloudflare fee, but ICANN rules still lock a domain for the usual 60 days after registration or after a registrant change.

com_first_year_usd.note: A new .com costs $10.46 for the first year, the live at-cost price Cloudflare shows in its own domain search, the same as what it pays the registry and ICANN.

com_renewal_usd.note: Renewal is the same $10.46 a year, since Cloudflare never marks up the price above what it pays.

whois_privacy_free.note: WHOIS redaction that hides your name and address from public records is on by default at no extra cost.

dns_included.note: DNS management is free, but every domain registered here must use Cloudflare's own nameservers, so you can't point it at another DNS provider without transferring the domain away first.

setup.step: Sign in to Cloudflare, search for the domain, and register it from the dashboard.
The domain becomes a Cloudflare DNS zone automatically; add an A or CNAME record pointing it at your host.
Add any SPF, DKIM or DMARC records your email service gives you in the same DNS app.

builder_notes: This domain must stay on Cloudflare's own nameservers while it's registered here, so manage its DNS records in the Cloudflare dashboard or API, not at another DNS host.
Add the host's DNS records and the email service's SPF, DKIM and DMARC records before assuming the site or outgoing email works.
If a script manages DNS through the Cloudflare API, keep the API token server-side and out of git.
